teams.heading: Tevita Tuiloa launches Coca-Cola cans celebrating iconic Fiji men's Sevens
teams.body: The Fiji men's national Sevens squad will be featured on limited-edition Coca-Cola cans and bottles to celebrate their iconic tournament performances. Officially launched at Albert Park in Suva, the commemorative collectables will highlight eight memorable moments from the team's 2025 Hong Kong and Singapore campaigns. Fiji Rugby commercial director Tevita Tuiloa welcomed the partnership, stating that the initiative celebrates the unique bond between the sport and local communities while inspiring future generations.

teams.heading: England hooker Jamie Blamire returns from injury to start for Leicester
teams.body: England hooker Jamie Blamire has recovered from injury to start for Leicester Tigers in the Slater Cup clash against Gloucester at Mattioli Woods Welford Road. The front-rower's return is one of five changes made by coach Geoff Parling following last weekend's victory over Newcastle. England international Freddie Steward retains his starting place at full-back, whilst scrum-half Jack van Poortvliet captains the side. Blamire's immediate return to fitness provides a welcome front-row boost ahead of next month's international fixtures.

lead.why: Jamie Blamire's return from injury to start for Leicester Tigers is the most significant selection event involving a senior England international today.

teams.heading: Victor Wembanyama credits French club Provence Rugby for inspiring team spirit
teams.body: French club Provence Rugby hosted NBA star Victor Wembanyama during his summer off-season, with the 7ft 4in Frenchman joining passing drills and line-outs to develop his physical strength. The 22-year-old San Antonio Spurs player, who was joined by team-mate Harrison Barnes, praised the second-tier side's unity and camaraderie. 'It was a great experience, seeing the team spirit they have over there,' Wembanyama said of his stint with Provence, who have started their promotion push with five consecutive league wins.

teams.heading: Munster appoint former Hurricanes chief Avan Lee as interim chief executive
teams.body: Munster have appointed former Hurricanes chief Avan Lee as their interim chief executive following the departure of Ian Flanagan. Lee, who previously led the Super Rugby franchise, steps in at Thomond Park while the province continues its search for a permanent successor. The experienced administrator has immediately expressed his desire to secure a future off-field role for Munster legend Peter O'Mahony once his playing career concludes.

teams.heading: Italy concede 318 points across their last 11 test matches
teams.body: Italy's men's national side have struggled for defensive stability, conceding 318 points across their last 11 fixtures. In that same 11-game window, the Azzurri scored 190 points, averaging 17.3 points scored per match. Their opponents averaged 28.9 points per game in those same 11 matches. The biggest victory for Italy in this 11-game block came when they beat Chile 34-19 at home in November 2025 during the international friendlies.

teams.heading: Marika Koroibete makes Ospreys debut as Fetuli Paea starts for Dragons
teams.body: The Ospreys hand a debut to Wallabies wing Marika Koroibete for tonight’s all-Welsh URC clash against the Dragons at Rodney Parade. Mark Jones’ side seek their first victory of the season following consecutive defeats in South Africa, while the hosts aim to build on a 38-26 win over the Scarlets. Dragons coach Filo Tiatia has handed a first start of the season to Tongan international Fetuli Paea at outside centre, with Huw Anderson and Harry Beddall also joining the starting XV.

teams.heading: Félix Páez Molina hails 2035 bid as vital for South American rugby
teams.body: Argentine Rugby Union president Félix Páez Molina has described the joint South American bid for the 2035 Rugby World Cup as a "very important step" for the region. Argentina are leading a four-nation consortium alongside Brazil, Chile and Uruguay, with technical information now submitted to World Rugby. The proposal includes 11 venues, such as the Estadio Monumental in Buenos Aires and the Maracanã in Rio de Janeiro. This first-ever South American bid faces competition from Spain, Italy and Japan, with a final decision expected in November 2027.

lead.why: UAR president Félix Páez Molina provided fresh comments on the bid's potential impact on the region.

teams.heading: Isaac Henry earns start as Joseph-Aukuso Suaalii remains on the wing
teams.body: Head coach Les Kiss has made just one enforced change to the starting XV for Saturday's opening Bledisloe Cup Test at Eden Park. Isaac Henry joins the midfield at outside centre to replace the suspended Hunter Paisami, with Len Ikitau shifting to inside centre. Despite his midfield pedigree, Joseph-Aukuso Suaalii retains his place on the wing following his successful first start there against South Africa. "Keeping consistency in the starting side gives us a solid foundation," Kiss noted, as he reverts to a 5-3 bench split.

teams.heading: Japan seek to overturn narrow one-point November defeat against Wales
teams.body: The Brave Blossoms return to action against Wales seeking to avenge their most recent meeting. The side currently sits 10th in the standings with one win and two losses from three rounds. Following a 15-42 loss to France, the squad carries a points difference of minus 26 into this fourth-round encounter.

teams.heading: Dave Rennie moves Damian McKenzie to fly-half as Richie Mo’unga withdraws
teams.body: Dave Rennie has shifted Damian McKenzie to fly-half for Saturday’s Bledisloe Cup opener after Richie Mo’unga was ruled out of the series with a calf tear. Mo’unga’s injury forces a backline reshuffle, with Beauden Barrett earning his first start of the year at full-back. Up front, former captain Scott Barrett returns to the engine room for his 90th Test following back surgery, while hooker Codie Taylor leads the side in Ardie Savea’s absence. Addressing his history with Australia, Rennie insisted "it’s not about me" despite his abrupt 2023 exit.

teams.heading: Eben Etzebeth returns to starting XV for Sharks' Stormers derby showdown
teams.body: Eben Etzebeth has been named in the Sharks' starting XV for Saturday’s United Rugby Championship clash against the Stormers in Cape Town. It marks the lock’s first start for the Durbanites this season following a cameo off the bench last weekend. He is joined in the run-on team by fellow Springboks Ox Nché and Ethan Hooker as head coach JP Pietersen looks to maintain his side’s perfect start to the campaign by ditching their previous bench-heavy rotation strategy.
